When a live book is stood down, main's startup reconcile_stale_twin_epochs closes its live_paper_twins row. If the SAME tag pair is later re-armed, sync_twin_epoch finds the existing closed row and returns it untouched: there is no code path that reopens a closed epoch or starts a new one for that tag. The pair therefore stays ended_at NOT NULL forever. OBSERVED IN PRODUCTION 2026-09-06: the contest-cap canary was stood down at 19:25Z (row closed) and re-armed at 23:51Z on Emmsell10/Emmsell10_pt4; the row stayed closed, the livedash (which reads live_paper_twins) showed the running real-money canary as RETIRED, and at that point every row in the table was closed. Trading was unaffected - the twin kept writing - so nothing errored and nothing alarmed. Impact is twofold: the operator cannot see a running live book, and parity reports scope to the epoch window so post-re-arm twin evidence is mis-scoped. Worked around for this canary by cutting a new epoch onto fresh tags (Fmmsell10/Fmmsell10_pt4, package mmsell-contestcap-epoch2, PR #360), which is the system's own prescribed remedy - a new twin tag is a new epoch - but the defect is general and affects any re-arm of any book after any stand-down.","classification":"OPS","owner_role":"LIVE_OPS","severity":"MEDIUM","priority":"P2","reason":"Live Ops runtime observation, outside the candidate detector surface: issue-candidates at 2026-09-08T07:15Z listed only the mmsell-price-ceiling drift and its two blocked gates, so OPEN_MANUAL rather than OPEN_CANDIDATE.
